We take this construction as the definition of `DP(α, H)`; Sethuraman's theorem that it has Ferguson's Dirichlet marginals is recorded in `WantedExt/Probability/DirichletProcessWanted.lean`.

nodes.summary: Mean of the Dirichlet process, law form: `∫ ν(A) dDP(α, H)(ν) = H(A)`.

nodes.summary: The moments of the Dirichlet process are the Blackwell–MacQueen urn (Blackwell–MacQueen 1973): `E[∏ᵢ G(Aᵢ)] = P(X₀ ∈ A₀, …, X_{n-1} ∈ A_{n-1})` for the urn's first `n` draws.
nodes.title: The moments of the Dirichlet process are the Blackwell–MacQueen urn

nodes.summary: Mean of the Dirichlet process (Ferguson 1973): `E[G(A)] = H(A)`.
nodes.title: Mean of the Dirichlet process

nodes.summary: If the pieces sum to `1` almost surely, then `E[G(A)] = H(A)` for every measurable `A`.
nodes.title: Mean of the random measure

nodes.summary: Mixed second moment of the Dirichlet process (Ferguson 1973): `E[G(A) G(B)] = (α H(A) H(B) + H(A ∩ B)) / (α + 1)`.
nodes.title: Mixed second moment of the Dirichlet process

nodes.summary: The Blackwell–MacQueen urn for two draws (Blackwell–MacQueen 1973): if `X₁, X₂` are i.i.d. draws from a Dirichlet process `G`, then `P(X₁ ∈ A, X₂ ∈ B) = E[G(A) G(B)]` equals `∫_A P(X₂ ∈ B | X₁ = x) dH(x)` with the predictive law `polyaUrnPredictive α H ![x] = (α H + δₓ) / (α + 1)`.
nodes.title: The Blackwell–MacQueen urn for two draws

nodes.summary: If the pieces sum to `1` almost surely, then `E[G(A) G(B)] = (1 - s) H(A) H(B) + s H(A ∩ B)` with `s = ∑ₖ E[πₖ²]` (`sumSqWeight`, at most `1` under this hypothesis): two draws from `G` pick the same piece with probability `s`, and otherwise land on two independent atoms.
nodes.title: Mixed second moment of the random measure

nodes.summary: Finite-dimensional marginals of the Dirichlet process (Ferguson 1973, §3; Sethuraman 1994, Theorem 3.4): on a measurable partition `A₀, …, A_m` of `X` with `H(Aᵢ) > 0`, the vector `(G(A₀), …, G(A_m))` has the Dirichlet law `Dir(α H(A₀), …, α H(A_m))`.
nodes.title: Finite-dimensional marginals of the Dirichlet process

nodes.summary: The predictive probability of a measurable set: `(α H(A) + #{i | xᵢ ∈ A}) / (α + n)`.
nodes.title: Predictive probability of a set in the Blackwell–MacQueen urn

nodes.summary: The predictive law in the Blackwell–MacQueen urn: after observations `x₀, …, x_{n-1}`, the next observation has law `(α H + ∑ᵢ δ_{xᵢ}) / (α + n)`. It is a probability measure for `α > 0` and a probability measure `H` (`isProbabilityMeasure_polyaUrnPredictive`); outside that domain the definition is total but meaningless (e.g. `α = n = 0` gives the zero measure).
nodes.title: Blackwell–MacQueen urn predictive law

nodes.summary: The random leftover stick `∏_{j<k} (1 - βⱼ)`.

nodes.summary: Ferguson's conjugacy (Ferguson 1973, Theorem 1): given `n` observations `xs` from `G ∼ DP(α, H)`, the posterior of `G` is `DP(α + n, (α H + ∑ᵢ δ_{xsᵢ}) / (α + n))`. Stated as the disintegration `P(G ∈ S, X₀ ∈ A₀, …) = ∫_{∏ Aᵢ} DP(α + n, posterior base)(S) dP(xs)` over the urn law of the observations.
nodes.title: Ferguson's conjugacy

nodes.summary: The product probability space `(ℕ → ℝ) × (ℕ → X)` carrying i.i.d. `Beta(1, α)` proportions and, independently, i.i.d. `H` atoms.
nodes.title: Sethuraman's canonical probability space

nodes.summary: Sethuraman's construction on the canonical space: the coordinates of the two factors are the proportions and the atoms.

nodes.title: Stick-breaking measure has total mass at most one

nodes.summary: The discrete measure `∑ₖ πₖ δ_{θₖ}` with the stick-breaking weights `πₖ = stickWeight b k` (negative weights, which do not occur for proportions in `[0, 1]`, are read as `0`).
nodes.title: Stick-breaking measure

nodes.summary: A stick-breaking process on the probability space `(Ω, μ)`: independent proportions `βₖ ∈ [0, 1]` (almost surely, with arbitrary laws), i.i.d. atoms `atom k` with law `H`, and the proportion sequence independent of the atom sequence. Ishwaran–James (2001) take `βₖ ∼ Beta(aₖ, bₖ)`; Sethuraman's Dirichlet process is `IsDirichlet`.
nodes.title: Stick-breaking process

nodes.summary: The leftover stick is in `[0, 1]` for proportions in `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Leftover stick lies in the unit interval

nodes.summary: The stick left after breaking off the first `k` pieces at proportions `b`: `∏_{j<k} (1 - bⱼ)`.
nodes.title: Leftover stick in stick breaking

nodes.summary: The pieces are nonnegative for proportions in `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of stick-breaking weights

nodes.summary: The `k`-th piece of a stick broken at proportions `b`: `bₖ ∏_{j<k} (1 - bⱼ)`.
nodes.title: Stick-breaking weights

nodes.summary: The first `n` pieces and the leftover stick make up the whole stick. Holds for all real `b`.
nodes.title: Stick-breaking pieces and leftover make up the whole stick

nodes.summary: Two draws from a Dirichlet process pick the same piece with probability `1 / (1 + α)`: `∑ₖ E[πₖ²] = 1 / (1 + α)`. This is the probability that the second customer of the Chinese restaurant process with parameter `α` joins the first one's table.
nodes.title: Probability that two Dirichlet process draws pick the same piece

nodes.summary: `∑ₖ E[πₖ²]`: given `G`, two independent draws from `G` pick the same piece `k` with probability `∑ₖ πₖ²`. For an atomless base measure the atoms are almost surely distinct, so this is also the probability that the two draws coincide (not used here).
nodes.title: Expected sum of squared stick-breaking weights

nodes.summary: Variance of the Dirichlet process (Ferguson 1973): `Var(G(A)) = H(A) (1 - H(A)) / (α + 1)`.
nodes.title: Variance of the Dirichlet process

nodes.summary: The random piece `πₖ = βₖ ∏_{j<k} (1 - βⱼ)`.
nodes.title: Random stick-breaking weight

conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.
